chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Abbad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah’s blessings be upon him and his family) said: There is not a morning except that two angels call out, saying: “O seeker of good, come! O seeker of evil, stop! Is there a supplicant so that he may be answered? Is there one who seeks forgiveness so that he may be forgiven? Is there a penitent so that he may be pardoned? Is there an anguished one so that his anguish may be relieved? O Allah, hasten for the one who spends his wealth a replacement, and for the one who withholds, ruin.” This is their supplication until the sun sets.

key_terms.الممسك: The one who withholds; the miser
key_terms.المنفق: The one who spends in charity; the generous
key_terms.باغي الخير: Seeker of good — one who strives toward righteous deeds
key_terms.باغي الشر: Seeker of evil — one who pursues sinful deeds
key_terms.تلفا: Ruin, loss, destruction — consequence of miserliness
key_terms.خلفا: Replacement, compensation — divine recompense for charity

ai.seo_question: What do the two angels say every morning according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) describes two angels who call out every morning, inviting people to do good and cease evil. The angels ask God to answer supplicants, forgive the repentant, relieve the distressed, and bestow blessings on those who spend charitably while bringing loss to the miserly. This hadith, narrated in a teaching assembly held on the last day of Rajab 368 AH, underscores the daily divine invitation to righteousness and the spiritual consequences of generosity versus miserliness.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi `Abdullah al-Barqi from his father from `Abbad b. Ya`qub from al-Husayn b. Zayd from Ja`far b. Muhammad al-Sadiq from his forefathers (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: There is not a morning except that two angels call out, saying: “O seeker of good, come. O seeker of evil, stop. Is there a supplicant so that he may be answered? Is there a repentant so that he may be forgiven? Is there a penitent so that he may be pardoned? Is there an anguished one so that he may be relieved of his anguish? O Allah! Hasten the replacement of the wealth of one who spends [in goodness] and destroy the one who withholds.” This is their supplication until sunset.
